video.title: New York Knicks Fantasy Basketball Preview [26/27 NBA Season]

summary: Josh Lloyd previews the 2026-27 fantasy outlook for the New York Knicks, the reigning NBA champions. He thinks repeating is hard. The East is stronger and the Knicks are weaker, so they may not be able to manage player minutes. He projects the starting five as Jalen Brunson, Mikal Bridges, Josh Hart, OG Anunoby and Karl-Anthony Towns. He calls Brunson overvalued in category leagues and Bridges one of his strongest fades. He says Towns is the best fantasy player on the team and Anunoby is good value in category leagues. Andre Drummond is the main stash because the team has almost no big-man depth. Overall he calls the Knicks a boring fantasy team with more fades than targets.

rules.text: Teams coming off a title often struggle the next regular season. They play two extra months, may be complacent, and may not value the regular season as much.
rules.quote: You have to play two months longer than most other teams. You win. There is complacency potentially.

rules.text: A strong conference can force a team to push its players harder and cut back on rest. That can raise injury risk.
rules.quote: And then they push harder and the push harder maybe gets to an injury.

rules.text: Do not draft a player based on his reputation or past real-life success. Judge him by what he actually produces in fantasy categories.
rules.quote: So, don't get wrapped up in the emotion, they said he'd never be good. Josh, you're just a hater.

rules.text: Playing next to a traditional center pushes a big man out to the perimeter. His rebounds, blocks and FG% usually drop.
rules.quote: play more on the perimeter. Rebounds down, blocks down, field goals down is the usual way it goes.

rules.text: Scoring format matters. A player's value can be very different in category leagues and points leagues, and between Yahoo and ESPN points.
rules.quote: So again, format is important and understanding what can and can't go wrong or change with a player

rules.text: Do not trust 9-cat rankings that inflate value. If a player's 9-cat rank looks great, do not assume the time he might miss is already priced in.

rules.text: Do not bump a mediocre player up 30 or 40 spots just for good health. Using that roster spot to stream waiver players can give more value.
